title: The Immutable Documents take precedence over any conflicting rule, decision or governance structure
content:
A.1.1.1 does two things beyond restating that the Spirit of the Atlas lives in the Immutable Documents. It establishes a **hierarchy of authority** — "The Immutable Documents take precedence over any other rules, decisions, or governance structures that may conflict with them" — and it establishes a **test of validity**: they "provide the definitive criteria for determining whether the Sky Ecosystem's rules and incentives are in harmony with Universal Alignment."

Precedence and criteria are different powers. Precedence resolves collisions: a governance vote, a facilitator action, or an Adaptive Document that conflicts with an Immutable Document loses, without needing a separate invalidation process. Criteria makes the Immutable Documents the reference against which alignment claims are adjudicated, which means an argument about whether something is aligned is always reducible to an argument about text rather than about taste.

The load-bearing part is that this closes the loop opened by the framework's own admission that Universal Alignment cannot be measured deterministically. If alignment is unmeasurable in the abstract, some concrete artefact must stand in as its operational definition — and A.1.1.1 nominates the Immutable Documents for that role. It is why the same documents can be simultaneously philosophical (enshrining a Spirit) and legalistic (supplying definitive criteria).
description: A.1.1.1 makes immutability also a conflict-resolution rule: the Immutable Documents are the definitive criteria for judging whether Sky's rules and incentives match Universal Alignment.
